<section class="ds-section" id="figures"><h2>What the data show</h2>
<h3>Trade values contracted sharply after 1929</h3>
<p>Between 1929 and 1933, annual export values fell by <strong>71.1%</strong> and import values by <strong>69.3%</strong>. Exports recovered to 58.5% of their 1929 value by 1937. These are changes in <em>current-price trade values</em>, not estimates of changes in physical trade volumes.</p>
<figure class="ds-figure"><img alt="Annual Czechoslovak exports and imports in current billion crowns from 1920 to 1938." decoding="async" loading="lazy" src="assets/files/datasets/figures/trade-annual.svg"/><figcaption>Source: <em>Annual totals</em>. The chart divides the workbook’s million-Kč values by 1,000; no price adjustment is applied.<span class="ds-image-links"><a download="" href="assets/files/datasets/foreign-trade-annual.csv">Chart data (CSV)</a> · <a href="assets/files/datasets/figures/trade-annual.svg">Open figure</a> · <a href="assets/files/datasets/figures/trade-annual.png">PNG</a></span></figcaption></figure>
<h3>The balance turned negative in 1932 and 1933</h3>
<p>The annual series records deficits of <strong>766.0 million Kč in 1932</strong> and <strong>202.2 million Kč in 1933</strong>, followed by a surplus of <strong>896.0 million Kč in 1934</strong>. A surplus alone does not establish an export-led recovery: it can also reflect falling imports.</p>
<figure class="ds-figure"><img alt="Czechoslovak annual exports minus imports, with negative balances in 1932 and 1933." decoding="async" loading="lazy" src="assets/files/datasets/figures/trade-balance.svg"/><figcaption>Source: <em>Annual totals</em>. Trade balance = exports − imports.<span class="ds-image-links"><a download="" href="assets/files/datasets/foreign-trade-annual.csv">Chart data (CSV)</a> · <a href="assets/files/datasets/figures/trade-balance.svg">Open figure</a> · <a href="assets/files/datasets/figures/trade-balance.png">PNG</a></span></figcaption></figure>
<h3>Monthly observations reveal movements hidden by annual totals</h3>
<p>The monthly table retains the supplied observations and their within-year variation. The chart applies no additional seasonal adjustment.</p>
<figure class="ds-figure"><img alt="Monthly national exports and imports in million crowns from January 1924 to December 1938." decoding="async" loading="lazy" src="assets/files/datasets/figures/trade-monthly.svg"/><figcaption>Source: <em>Monthly totals</em>.<span class="ds-image-links"><a download="" href="assets/files/datasets/foreign-trade-monthly.csv">Chart data (CSV)</a> · <a href="assets/files/datasets/figures/trade-monthly.svg">Open figure</a> · <a href="assets/files/datasets/figures/trade-monthly.png">PNG</a></span></figcaption></figure>
<h3>The distribution of exports changed</h3>
<p>Germany’s share of national exports declined from 22.89% in 1929 to 15.05% in 1937; Austria’s declined from 15.00% to 7.32%. The figure follows the five largest destinations in the supplied 1929 partner table, keeping the same selection in 1937.</p>
<figure class="ds-figure"><img alt="Export shares in 1929 and 1937 for Germany, Austria, the United States, the United Kingdom and Hungary." decoding="async" loading="lazy" src="assets/files/datasets/figures/trade-partners.svg"/><figcaption>Source: <em>Annual partners</em>. Shares use national exports as the denominator, not exports to the selected five countries.<span class="ds-image-links"><a download="" href="assets/files/datasets/foreign-trade-partners.csv">Chart data (CSV)</a> · <a href="assets/files/datasets/figures/trade-partners.svg">Open figure</a> · <a href="assets/files/datasets/figures/trade-partners.png">PNG</a></span></figcaption></figure>

<section class="ds-section" id="coverage"><h2>Coverage and units</h2>
<div class="ds-table-scroll"><table class="ds-table"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Sheet</th><th scope="col">Observations</th><th scope="col">Contents</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Annual totals</td><td>19 years</td><td>National exports, imports, balance, turnover, export–import ratio, growth rates and 1929-based indices.</td></tr><tr><td>Annual partners</td><td>285 partner-years</td><td>Exports, imports, bilateral balances and shares of national trade for fifteen partners.</td></tr><tr><td>Monthly totals</td><td>180 months</td><td>National totals and derived indicators; no monthly bilateral panel is included.</td></tr><tr><td>Monthly analysis extension</td><td>180 months × 6 methods</td><td>Observed flows, three trailing averages, a centered average and an HP trend, with consistently derived balances and ratios.</td></tr><tr><td>Charts</td><td>Visual summaries</td><td>Workbook charts and their source tables.</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p>Trade values are stored in <strong>million current Kč</strong>. Balance is exports minus imports; turnover is their sum. Ratios, shares and growth columns are expressed as percentage numbers. Annual indices use the annual 1929 value; monthly indices use the mean month of 1929.</p>
<details><summary>Included partners</summary><p>Austria; Belgium and Luxembourg; France; Germany; Hungary; Italy; Netherlands; Poland; Romania; Sweden; Switzerland; USSR; United Kingdom; United States; Yugoslavia.</p><p>The partner table is not exhaustive. Its shares need not sum to 100%. It is distinct from the fourteen-partner basket used in the <a href="czechoslovakia-eer.html">EER dataset</a>.</p></details>
<p class="ds-small">All figures use observations from the supplied workbook. The monthly analysis extension is dated 13 November 2026; source observations retain their original units and values.</p>
</section>

<section class="ds-section" id="monthly-methods"><h2>How the monthly indicators are constructed</h2>
<p>Let <strong>X</strong> denote exports and <strong>M</strong> imports. For a smoothed view, the selected filter is applied to each flow first. The other indicators are then calculated from those same smoothed flows.</p>
<div class="ds-table-scroll"><table class="ds-table"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Indicator</th><th scope="col">Definition</th><th scope="col">How to read it</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>Trade balance</td><td>X − M</td><td>Million current Kč; positive means a surplus and negative a deficit.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Export coverage of imports</td><td>100 × X / M</td><td>100% means exports equal imports; 120% means exports are 1.2 times imports.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Normalized trade balance</td><td>100 × (X − M) / (X + M)</td><td>Balance as a percentage of total trade; zero denotes balanced trade.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Total trade</td><td>X + M</td><td>Combined exports and imports in million current Kč.</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
<p>A smoothed export/import ratio is therefore a <strong>ratio of smoothed flows</strong>, rather than an average of monthly ratios. For the 12-month trailing average, it also equals the ratio of exports to imports summed over those twelve months.</p>
<details><summary>Moving averages, HP settings and unavailable values</summary>
<ul><li><strong>Trailing averages:</strong> the mean of the current month and the preceding 2, 5 or 11 months. All months in a window must be observed. These averages delay turning points; the 12-month option first becomes available in December 1924.</li>
<li><strong>Centered 12-month average:</strong> a standard 2 × 12-month average. It uses thirteen observations, with half-weight on each endpoint: weights 1/24 at t − 6 and t + 6, and 1/12 for each of the eleven intervening months. Six months at each end have no centered estimate.</li>
<li><strong>HP trend:</strong> the Hodrick–Prescott filter in levels, with monthly λ = 129,600, following the frequency adjustment of Ravn and Uhlig (2002). It uses the full available monthly sample; the date controls change the displayed interval without re-estimating the trend.</li>
<li><strong>Missing values:</strong> unavailable values remain blank, and ratios require a positive denominator. Moving averages require complete calendar windows. If future source data contain gaps, HP is fitted separately to common observed runs of at least 24 months.</li></ul>
<p>HP trends are descriptive smooth estimates. They use observations on both sides of a date and can be sensitive near sample boundaries and abrupt changes. Smoothing does not adjust for prices, perform a full seasonal adjustment or resolve changes in statistical coverage.</p>
</details>
<p class="ds-small">Method references: <a href="https://doi.org/10.1162/003465302317411604">Ravn and Uhlig (2002), <em>Review of Economics and Statistics</em> 84(2), 371–376</a>; <a href="https://otexts.com/fpp3/decomposition.html#moving-averages">Hyndman and Athanasopoulos, <em>Forecasting: Principles and Practice</em>, moving averages</a>. The <a href="assets/files/datasets/foreign-trade-analysis/README.txt">analysis documentation</a> includes the exact formulas, source checksum and reproduction instructions.</p>
</section>
